decisions.text: No WebView; Studio links open the system browser through the foundation's web-link mapping.

Home is the Auto thread with the server's needs-you rows above it (the handoff's `needs` variant 2a); older chats sit behind a list button; the morning digest will arrive as Auto's message in the same thread (A4, nothing to build here).
Pill input, round send/stop button, [+] for camera, photo library and files; Return inserts a newline; the button sends or stops; NO suggestion chips.
No Plan toggle: never send planMode or missionMode. Auto's own cards render and work in the thread as in Studio.

Mission suggestion (file it → POST /api/missions), plan approval (mission_approval → POST /api/missions/{id}/approve | /reject), tool approval (tool_approval → POST /api/v1/approval-grants/{id}/grant | /deny), task card, withdraw offer (Withdraw = deny the grant, Keep it = nothing), limit and attachment notices. Each refuses honestly when the role cannot act.

'Ask Auto about #0419' opens a NEW conversation with the ticket in the request's page context (the web's Discuss, vendored lib/discussion.ts) and offers 'Update ticket and re-queue' (POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/rebrief).
Stop cancels on the server (POST /api/chat/{chat_id}/cancel) as well as aborting the read; dropping the connection alone never cancels a turn.

A stale chat id silently creates a new chat on the server, so GET /api/chat/{id} is checked before a cached id is reused; reopening a chat whose turn is in flight shows 'Auto is working…' and refetches on chat_changed.
The foundation's AiLabel sits by the composer on every chat screen, in its fixed colours; while useAiLabelVisible() is false the composer is disabled with the vendored paused text.
Viewers get history read-only with 'Ask your workspace owner for editor access to talk to Auto' and a disabled composer; owners, admins and editors chat and act on cards (src/auth/role.ts roleCan).

Nothing about plans, credits or prices: limit_reached frames and trial_exhausted / rate_limited errors render this kit's fixed copy (e.g. 'Auto has reached a limit for now. Ask your workspace owner.'), never a server string that may name a plan.
Chat message bodies are never persisted (the foundation's persister excludes the chat families; do not add a second store).
All HTTP through the foundation's src/api client and stream; zod at every boundary; unknown frames and fields ignored.
Files 200-400 lines (never over 800), functions under 50, components under 150, nesting under 4; pure logic in plain TS with tests; immutability; tokens only.
No dependency, native module, config plugin or app.json change in this wave (package.json, package-lock.json, app.json, eas.json untouched — gate-enforced).

This kit may create or change ONLY: src/chat/**, app/(app)/index.tsx (replaces the foundation's placeholder home), app/(app)/chat/**, app/(app)/chats.tsx, and its own kit files under scripts/ralph/. Everything else — src/api, src/auth, src/core, src/styles, src/ui, src/navigation, src/storage, app/_layout.tsx, app/(app)/_layout.tsx, app/(app)/cc/**, app/(app)/settings/**, src/cc/**, package.json, app.json, .github — belongs to the foundation or the A3 kit (gate-enforced allowlist).

The foundation's contracts are fixed for this wave. If one is missing or wrong, build the smallest feature-local adapter under src/chat/ and write 'FOUNDATION GAP: <what, where>' in the story's DONE mark; never edit a foundation file. A missing UI primitive is built feature-local under src/chat/components/.

Every server path this wave calls is a constant in src/chat/routes.ts (the route check reads it); a route PRD-266 adds is marked pendingUpstream. App navigation uses the foundation's src/navigation/routes.ts builders only (cc.questions, cc.ticket(taskId), cc.social(postId), settings, chat(id), chats).

The home thread is the newest conversation from GET /api/chat/history after the stale check, or a draft with no id; the first message of a draft creates the chat and the chat-id frame tells the app its id. 'New chat' starts a draft.
Auto's answer renders as plain text with paragraphs, as the handoff draws it (14/1.55, no bubble); a markdown renderer would be a new dependency and is not in this wave (open question for Gerard).
